**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve tool inputs beyond the decoder nesting limit**

When a Bedrock model emits a valid JSON tool argument nested roughly 1,000 levels on supported Python 3.10/3.11, `json.loads` raises `RecursionError`, which bypasses this `ValueError` handler. `_finish` invokes this after setting `_finished` and from the generator's `else` path, so the exception escapes the final `next()` and leaves the span unlogged even though the Bedrock stream completed successfully; decoder-limit failures should fall back to the raw string too.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L17-L20](https://github.com/braintrustdata/braintrust-sdk-python/blob/dd8c819a331f0f459a6dfde8000dd0a7e225a5ef/AGENTS.md#L17-L20)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Valid, thanks. Fixed in 9477af1: `_parse_streamed_tool_input` now also falls back to the raw string on `RecursionError`, as `harbor/identity.py` already does, with a unit test for a 100,000-level nested input.
